in_arabic.name: حمزة
in_arabic.meaning: اسم حمزة يعني القوة و الشجاعة في اللغة العربية
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم حمزة هو اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي و يعني القوة و الشجاعة، و هو من الأسماء التي تطلق على الأسد في اللغة العربية. و يعتبر حمزة من الأسماء المحببة في الإسلام و ذلك لكونه اسم أحد أصحاب النبي محمد صلى الله عليه و سلم و هو حمزة بن عبد المطلب، و يعتبر من الأسماء التي تحمل معاني القوة و الصبر و الثبات.

in_pashto.name: حمزه
in_pashto.meaning: حمزه د قوي او زړور نوم دی
in_pashto.long_meaning: حمزه يو مذکر نوم دی چي د عربي ژبې څخه اخستل شوی دی او د قوي او زړور معنی لري. دا نوم د افغان او پښتون قومونو لپاره ډير اهميت لري ځکه چي حمزه بن عبدالمطلب د پښتنو د افتخار يو له سترګو شمېرل کيږي.

The name reflects attributes of strength, courage, and steadfastness, making it a popular choice among Muslim communities worldwide.

data.cultural_impact: The Islamic name "Hamzah" holds a significant cultural impact as it is the third letter of the Arabic alphabet and is represented by a 'dot below'. This symbol holds historical and traditional significance, as it was believed to be the first letter learned by the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) when he started learning to read the Quran. The name also holds an honorable place in Islamic history being the name of several esteemed figures such as Hamzah ibn Abdul-Muttalib, the uncle of Muhammad (PBUH), and Hamzah ibn Ahmad, one of the ten Promised Paradise martyrs.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Hamzah" holds great spiritual significance as it is derived from the Arabic root word "humaza," which means to be steadfast and determined. It reflects the spirit of courage, endurance, and defiance against hardships. The name is also a reminder of the importance of having unwavering faith and determination in Allah's path. In Islamic tradition, Hamza, the uncle of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), is remembered as a brave warrior who went above and beyond to protect Islam and its people. His unwavering commitment and courage illustrate the spiritual qualities that become a source of inspiration for believers to this day.
